newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LME copper shorts are hedge - LG Metals.
newsitem.headline: LME copper shorts are hedge - LG Metals.

text.p: Copper short positions held by South Korea's LG Metals Group on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are hedging positions for physical stocks carried over from last year, Hong Seong-ho, team manager for aluminium sales and LME operations told Reuters on Wednesday.
He added that LG Metals had not asked its LME brokers for an increase in its credit lines and that it had not received margin calls on its metals trading.

When asked to confirm rumours in the London base metals market that LG Metals' running copper short positions on the LME totalled between 100,000 and 200,000 tonnes of copper, Hong did not comment on the size of his company's positions.
"Yes, we have some (short positions). They are hedging positions for our physical stocks which have been carried over from last year," he said.
"We have not asked our LME brokers to increase our current credit lines," Hong said, adding "And also we have not been asked for margin calls by our brokers."

Hong said he was not aware that LG Metals had received a letter from the chief executive of the LME, David King, expressing concern about the company's operations on the exchange, as reported by some metal traders.
"I don't know whether the president of my company received a letter from the LME or not," he said.
King could not be reached by Reuters in London on either Monday or Tuesday to confirm the existence of any letter.

London metal dealers said LG Metals had been caught heavily short during a period of extreme supply tightness for prompt copper positions on the LME which has sent the backwardation on the contract soaring and driven borrowing rates sky-high.

When LME copper trading closed on Tuesday, the contract's backwardation, the premium of cash to three month metal, was indicated at $330/$340 a tonne - equal to the levels reached during the Sumitomo-induced tightness of May last year and December 1995.

Cash/one day traded at a premium of $24, just under the permissible daily limit, as major shorts between now and next week continued to be squeezed. Cash/one week traded at $110, while cash/February was a steep $265 traded.
LME three month copper was quoted at $2,241/46 a tonne in late Asian trade on Wednesday, virtually unchanged from Tuesday afternoon's kerb close of $2,244.
